recheck.why: Lint is 1.000 and clean, all 8 slots are spent, the budget arithmetic is exact (1 Glob, 5 Greps, 4 Reads, plus 2 declared out-of-budget Greps in step 7), role/level are exactly ams-verification-engineer/junior, and most of the analog content is genuinely good. But step 1 — the step that establishes the skill's whole premise — teaches an invalid inference and contradicts step 7. Step 1 says: "Then one Grep of that log whose pattern alternates the profile's Pass marker with the string from the Check macro slot. This procedure exists for one result: the pass marker present, zero check-macro lines — not a passing test, a test with no opinion." But the skill defines that string twice as a FAILURE string: "Check macro narrows Fatal markers to what an analog behavioural check prints when it fires", and the slot asks for "the macro or task our behavioural checks report through ... and whether it counts toward the run's error total". A passing run prints zero fire-lines whether or not any checks exist, so the Grep cannot distinguish "nothing is comparing the analog behaviour" from "twelve good checks all passed" — the exact distinction the skill exists to make. Step 7 confirms the failure-string semantics and contradicts step 1 head-on: it requires the string "absent in the first and present in the second", i.e. the same absence is step 7's expected clean baseline and step 1's proof of a vacuum. Only one can be right and step 7 matches the slot text; step 1's second half is both unsound and redundant with step 3, which greps the macro across testbench SOURCE and is the correct way to answer the question. This assumes a house-convention fact (that the macro emits on a passing evaluation) that is not a slot and that the skill's own slot text denies. Secondary: falsified : yes | no | not-yet-run is the registered T1 enum `fired : confirmed | not-confirmed | not-run` ("whether the authored checker was observed to fire on the stimulus written to provoke it") under a different name with disjoint spellings — C008 cannot catch it because the values were renamed too — and `falsified` is simultaneously a VALUE of the registered `proof status` where it means a property was refuted, i.e. the opposite polarity.
remaining: BLOCKING — step 1 (lines 89-97): the Grep for the Check macro string in a PASSING log cannot prove nothing is checked. The skill defines that string as what a check prints 'when it fires' (line 55) and as narrowing Fatal markers, and the slot (line 48) asks whether it 'counts toward the run's error total'. A passing run prints zero such lines whether or not checks exist. Keep the Pass-marker half (confirming the test really passed) and delete the zero-check-lines inference; step 3's source Grep already answers 'is anything comparing this' correctly.

BLOCKING — step 1 contradicts step 7 (lines 188-191). Step 7 requires the Check macro string 'absent in the first' run, i.e. the unperturbed passing run — precisely the absence step 1 reads as proof of a vacuum. The two steps require opposite behaviours of the same string; reconcile them explicitly in the text so a reader cannot be caught between them.

Handoff drift — 'falsified : yes | no | not-yet-run' (line 202) is the registered T1 enum 'fired : confirmed | not-confirmed | not-run' (same question, same object, 1:1 value map) under a new name with disjoint spellings. Either rename to 'fired' and copy the values verbatim, or state in prose why the one-column test fails. Also note 'falsified' is already a value of the registered 'proof status' meaning a property was refuted (bad news), whereas 'falsified: yes' here means the check is trustworthy — inverted polarity on the same word inside one pack.

signature (line 203) has no step that supplies 'kind'. Step 7's Grep yields the fired line so 'what'/'where' are reachable, but the schema's kind enum (assert scoreboard timeout xprop fatal uvm-error tool) has no token for a procedural behavioural checker, which step 6 explicitly permits via the Assertion support slot. Say which token applies, or say plainly it stays '?'.

Step 3 overclaim (line 106): 'One Grep for the Check macro slot's macro across the testbench gives every site that compares anything.' It gives every site reporting THROUGH that macro; a comparison reporting via the simulator's own error task or a UVM error is invisible, so a genuinely checked net can be misfiled as sampled-not-compared. Soften the claim and add that limitation to the 'coverage' line.

The description advertises 'when a comparator check chatters on ripple', but step 1 admits only the zero-check-lines case (a chattering check floods the log with them) and step 4 (line 120) restricts the draft to 'sampled-not-compared' or 'untouched' nets — a chattering net is 'checked'. Either give that trigger a path through the procedure or drop it from the description.
new_problems: Step 1's Grep of a passing log for the Check macro string is an unsound inference: the slot text (line 48) and the narrowing paragraph (line 55) both define that string as what a check prints when it FIRES, so a passing run yields zero lines regardless of whether any checks exist. The step therefore cannot establish the premise the entire skill rests on, and it burns 1 of the 5 budgeted Greps doing it.

Step 1 and step 7 require opposite behaviours of the same Check macro string within four steps of each other: step 7 treats its absence in the unperturbed passing run as the expected clean baseline, step 1 treats the same absence as proof that nothing is checked.

'falsified : yes | no | not-yet-run' restates the registered enum 'fired : confirmed | not-confirmed | not-run' under a different name with disjoint spellings — invisible to C008 because the values were renamed too — and collides in polarity with 'proof status: falsified', which in dv-formal-apps and dv-formal-overconstraint-credit means a property was refuted.
